summary: @c1-ease/autoloan postinstall beacon exfiltrates host metadata to unrelated VPS
details: The package self-describes as a 'compatibility shim' and its main entry returns a no-op Proxy, but its only real behavior is an install-time and require-time beacon. beacon.cjs reads os.hostname(), __dirname, process.cwd(), process.version, and the package name, and POSTs them over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false). The beacon fires automatically from the postinstall lifecycle script on npm install and again on require() of the main module. The destination is an unrelated bare Contabo VPS, not infrastructure associated with the declared scope. The package name, implausibly high 99.0.1 version, and stub body are consistent with a dependency-confusion probe against an internal @c1-ease scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
